jobs.title: Surveyor I
jobs.description:
Job Description

The Surveyor I is an entry or junior-level position for new graduates and/or those candidates with less than five (5) years of experience in an applicable industry. The Surveyor I, under a direct supervisor, performs work involving conventional surveying practices. The primary function is to develop the ability to effectively examine and report on vessels and other marine structures during and after construction relative to compliance with the applicable requirements for maintaining the vessel in Classification with ABS and meeting associated statutory and special service requirements related to Safety of Life at Sea, Loadline, Tonnage, Cargo Gear and Pollution Prevention Certification.

What You Will Do (with the assistance and guidance of an experienced ABS Surveyor):

  • Acts as a professional specialist for the organization in the application of related rules, regulations, requirements, concepts, principles, and processes.
  • Performs routine surveys on classed vessels, platforms, or other marine structures and at manufacturers for classification and compliance with statutory requirements.
  • Prepares technically accurate and timely reports of inspections and surveys performed.
  • Engages in contact with clients to resolve problems within areas of expertise.
  • Maintains survey files in an orderly and up-to-date manner in the area of responsibility.
  • Develops the skills necessary for the administration of office procedures and monitoring of business performance at an assigned port.
  • Through broader and more technically challenging work assignments, the individual must develop a thorough understanding of field operations, policies, methods, and procedures.

What You Will Need:

Education and Experience

  • Qualifications from a tertiary institution within a relevant field of engineering or physical science (minimum two (2) years program); or
  • Qualifications from a marine or nautical institution and relevant seagoing experience as a certificated ship officer, and
  • Proficiency in the English language commensurate with the scope of statutory certification and services and, before assignment, with their future work.
  • Appropriate certification and/or licenses in areas of specialization may be required.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

  • Ability to develop a working knowledge of ABS Rules, Guides, statutory regulations, and related instructions, as well as the ABS Employee Safety Policy.
  • Ability to read engineering plans and have a basic understanding of shipbuilding practices and vessel operations.
  • Ability to perform surveys in the prescribed format.
  • Knowledge of computer programs or software packages related to job responsibilities.
  • Knowledge of related technical interfaces required for group project work.
  • Knowledge of ships' engineering systems and machinery.
  • Ability to communicate, orally and in writing, pertinent information relative to assigned area of technical expertise.
  • Ability to analyze problems and propose solutions.
  • Responsiveness to customers and the ability to work well with others.
  • Ability to become familiar with the ABS Health, Safety, Quality, and Environmental Management Systems.

Physical Requirements:

  • Where allowed by local laws, a pre-employment physical examination is mandatory.
  • The role of surveyor/auditor requires sufficient physical strength, stamina, agility, and both visual and auditory acuity to perform the listed duties effectively.
  • The ability to climb vertical ladders up to nine meters and navigate steep steps is essential.
  • Shall be capable of working at heights on various staging and lifting equipment.
  • Shall be able to maneuver in tight spaces and work inside confined areas for extended periods, including kneeling and crawling.
  • The role may involve exposure to industrial environments, potential injury risks, extreme weather conditions, and demanding physical activities.
  • Shall be able to lift at least 25 lbs. / 11.34 kgs.
  • The use of small tools and the wearing of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), in accordance with ABS safety procedures, may be required.
  • Where allowed by local laws, the surveyor will be required to successfully complete an annual physical that will recertify the individual can perform the physical actions required.

Reporting Relationships:

Will report to the Principal, Senior, or Surveyor-in-Charge of the assigned port. This position does not have any direct reports.

About Us

We set out more than 160 years ago to promote the security of life and property at sea and preserve the natural environment. Today, we remain true to our mission and continue to support organizations facing a rapidly evolving seascape of challenging regulations and new technologies. Through it all, we are anchored by a vision and mission that help our clients find clarity in uncertain times.

ABS is a global leader in marine and offshore classification and other innovative safety, quality, and environmental services. Weâre at the forefront of supporting the global energy transition at sea, the application of remote and autonomous marine systems, cutting-edge technical solutions, and many more exciting advancements. Our commitment to safety, reliability, and efficiency is ever-present, guiding our clients to safer and more efficient operations.

jobs.title: Why do you want this new job
jobs.description:
No matter which side of the table youâve sat during interviews, youâve probably heard this question: âWhy do you want this new job?â

In the recent past, Iâve interviewed a few candidates and heard the following answers so far:

  • Iâm not learning much on the current job after itâs been 2-4 years.
  • Iâm looking for something that offers better work-life balance.
  • Iâm not really looking for a job. The recruiters got in touch and I thought Iâd discuss.
  • Iâm looking for more challenging work.

All of the above are valid answers. I think thereâs another perfectly valid answer that candidates seldom mention probably due to the gravity of the interview room situation. Iâve interviewed over a hundred candidates across different companies and am yet to find anyone that mentions: I am not happy with my current salary and benefits compared to my skills

Back to topic of answers. So, when someone answers that they are not learning new things on the job, obviously, youâd be curios to know why and how they have tried to change things. Unfortunately, most candidates simply mention that they are doing repeat work and thereâs not much to learn doing the same thing over and over again. This is where I start feeling a little uneasy. However, I understand that itâs a true statement. If youâre in a similar situation, hereâs some suggestion: read books, and write code based on what youâve read. Then, you can tell a much convincing story that, Iâve forced myself to learn new things and hereâs some proof, but I really want to apply the newly learned skills outside the scope of the âhello worldâ skills.

About work-life balance, I totally hear you. And if your current job doesnât suit what you need out of your life, itâs a perfectly valid reason to look for new opportunities. However, make sure youâre able to clearly set the expectation with your potential employer about what work-life balance means for you. For example, if you canât work over 40 hours a week, or must work from home one-two days a week, itâs best to discuss this even before an interview starts to ensure youâre a good match with the employer.

If you showed up at in interview just because a recruiter got in touch, Iâd say introspect first. Itâs possible that on our subconcious mind you have expectations that the potential of the new job offers you something that you donât get at the current job. So, instead of a passive asnwer that the you simply acted based on the recruiterâs invite, itâs much convincing to see if you can lay down one or two things that you expect from the new job that you donât get at the current job.

About looking for more challenge, it sounds like a cliche unless you can share examples of work that is of challenging to you. May be you like the challenge of using more complicated algorithms, may be you like dealing with a lot of data, may be you like supporting production emergencies, but thereâs gotta be something that you can explicitly mention as challenging. It helps employers to understand if theyâre able to provide you with enough challenge on the job.

Finally, if youâre looking for a new job because the current job isnât paying upto the level of your skills and contributions, make sure to communicate it clearly as well. With salaries and benefits, I find it much easier to work with people that know the actual $ figure thatâll make them happy instead of beating around the bush to create confusions all around. Just be confident and tell what makes you happy. If the employer can afford it, most likely theyâll want to get you onboard as a happy employee. If they canât afford it, theyâll do their best. The key here is to be explicit about what you want and be sure and confident about it.

In a nutshell, when you walk into an interview itâs yours to lose. The potential employer is investing their time and resources and would rather have you hired than having to interview other candidates. As long as you are able to justify why you want the new job, theyâll be quite accommodating.

About The Role

You'll be our first Head of Security. There's already a real foundation hereâbug bounty, pen tests, automated code and configuration scanning on the production and code side, phishing simulations on the people side. Youâll add to it across access and identity, SecOps and monitoring, incident response, vendor security, employee security practices, and policy. You'll own the whole posture.

This is a player-coach role. Early on, you'll do the scoping and the hands-on work yourself; this is not a role where you direct from above. As the work demands it, we're fully prepared to build a team hereâand we're looking to you to define what that team should be and when.

You'll report to the VP of Engineering, Tremendous' most senior technical leader. We've deliberately placed security with Engineering so you're set up to drive real implementation fastâembedded with the people whose work you're securing, not siloed in a compliance function. As the security function matures, we'll revisit this.

What You'll Do

  • Own Tremendous' security posture end-to-end, partnering with our engineering team on production infrastructure and code security.
  • Assess where we have gaps, prioritize them, and tackle our highest-leverage gaps first. Weâll have opinions, but you own the prioritization and implementation.
  • Treat incident response as core, not afterthought. We may not be able to prevent a breach, but your job is making sure it's small, contained, and that we know exactly what to do.
  • Drive security as a cultural shift across the companyâintroducing controls incrementally, working with teams rather than over them. "Yes, and," not "no."

What You'll Bring

What's Cool About The Role

 Arabian Private Holdings was founded on the principle that many critical business problems do not fit the traditional large-firm consulting model. A board facing a succession question or a family group weighing a capital injection does not need a team of twelve associates and a hundred-page methodology deck. They need experienced partners who can sit with a problem, form a rigorous view, and defend it. We take on a limited number of mandates to ensure that every client receives direct attention from the principals who are actually accountable for the outcome. Our work covers corporate strategy, governance, and operating model efficiency for some of the most significant family groups, listed corporations, and government entities in the region. We focus on clarity over complexity. Preferred Qualifications

  • Supportive and collaborative team culture.

  • Performance recognition and advancement opportunities.

The ideal candidate consistently delivers accurate work, meets deadlines, maintains confidentiality, communicates effectively with colleagues, and demonstrates a proactive approach to improving data quality and administrative processes.

PulseMediaNL is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all employees are treated with respect and provided equal opportunities.

jobs.description:
150.000 € Werbebudget pro Woche in der Peakzeit. Und der Plan ist, dass es mehr wird.

Valkental entwickelt seit 2020 Outdoorprodukte für mehr Sicherheit und Komfort im Straßenverkehr. Über 400.000 Kunden vertrauen bereits auf uns. Unser Shop ist achtstellig. Deine Aufgabe ist es, ihn auf dem Weg zu einem neunstelligen zu begleiten.

Unsere Meta- und Google-Accounts steuert bisher einer der Gründer und Geschäftsführer. Jetzt übergibt er sie. Und zwar an dich. Du übernimmst rund 500.000 € Ad-Spend im Monat, in Vollzeit, 100 % remote und mit direktem Draht zur Geschäftsführung. Dein Job: den Account profitabel skalieren.

Aufgaben

Kurzfassung: Du siehst jeden Tag als Erstes, was im Account passiert, und entscheidest, was als Nächstes kommt. Für den Account. Für die Creatives. Für das Wachstum.

  • Du steuerst Meta und Google täglich: Budgets, Struktur (ABO/CBO), Gebotsstrategien, Kill oder Promote.
  • Du skalierst profitabel und findest Wege, mehr Spend bei gleichem NC-ROAS auszugeben.
  • Du fährst Sales-Events wie die Black Week mit sechsstelligem Budget selbst.
  • Du analysierst die Performance in Triple Whale, Meta, Google und Shopify und gibst deine Learnings direkt an unsere Creative Strategists weiter.
  • Du baust unser wöchentliches KPI-Reporting über alle Kanäle auf.
  • Du entwickelst unsere Automationen mit KI-Routinen weiter und testest neue Kanäle.

Qualifikation

  • Mindestens 2 Jahre Media Buying bei einer E-Commerce-Brand oder Performance-Agentur, mit eigener Budgetverantwortung.
  • Meta Ads beherrschst du sicher: Du hast Accounts eigenständig gesteuert und skaliert und weißt, wie Gebotsstrategien, Zielgruppen und Attribution zusammenspielen.
  • Du hast Budgets verantwortet, bei denen ein Fehler weh tut: mindestens fünfstellig im Monat, mindestens ein sechsstelliges Sales-Event.
  • Google Ads (Search, Shopping, PMax) kannst du bereits oder lernst du schnell.
  • Du denkst in Zahlen (Triple Whale oder vergleichbar, MER, Post-Purchase-Survey) und nutzt KI selbstverständlich für Analysen und Automationen.
  • Du arbeitest genau und triffst trotzdem mutige Budgetentscheidungen, wenn es ums Skalieren geht.
  • Du bist bereit, auch am Wochenende zu arbeiten: Der Account wird jeden Tag geprüft. Auch samstags. Auch sonntags.
  • Du sprichst fließend Deutsch und gutes Englisch.

Benefits

  • Ein Account, mit dem du wirklich arbeiten kannst: rund 500.000 € Ad-Spend im Monat. Tendenz steigend.
  • Echte Verantwortung ab Tag eins: Du fährst den Account eigenständig.
  • Klare Entwicklungsperspektive: Wer kann und will, wächst bei uns Richtung Senior oder Head of Marketing.
  • Gehalt nach Erfahrung (nach oben offen).
  • 100 % Remote: Du arbeitest von wo du willst, solange du in Europa lebst und erreichbar bist.
  • Flexible Arbeitszeiten: Du teilst dir deinen Tag selbst ein, solange der Account täglich gecheckt ist.
  • Direkter Draht zur Geschäftsführung: Du sprichst mit den Leuten, die entscheiden.
  • Technik-Setup deiner Wahl.
  • Zugang zu Corporate Benefits.
  • Ehrliches, direktes Feedback, das dich schneller weiterbringt.
  • Ein bis zwei Teamevents im Jahr.

Klingt das nach dir? Dann brauchen wir kein Anschreiben. Zeig uns lieber Zahlen: Welche Accounts hast du gesteuert, mit welchen Monatsbudgets und mit welchen Ergebnissen (NC-ROAS, MER, CPA)? Welches Sales-Event hast du selbst gefahren?

Praktisch: Deinen Lebenslauf lädst du unter „CV“ hoch. Alles andere (Zahlen, Screenshots, ein kurzes Wort zu dir) packst du ins Anschreiben-Feld (max. 10 MB).

Wichtig: Bewerbungen ohne konkrete Accounts und Zahlen sortieren wir aus.

Wenn du dir vorher ein Bild von uns machen willst: Auf unserer Karriereseite lernst du das Team kennen.

Tabea und das Valkental-Team freuen sich auf dich!

jobs.title: Director, GTM & Revenue Operations
jobs.description:
THE CARWOW GROUP

Carwow Group is driven by a passion for getting people into cars. But not just any car, the right car. That’s why we are building the go-to destination for car-changing, whether you are looking to buy, sell or lease. Designed to reach drivers everywhere with our trail-blazing portfolio of personality rich automotive brands; Carwow, Auto Express, evo, Driving Electric and Car Buyer.

What started as a simple reviews site, is now one of the largest online car-changing destinations in Europe. Last year alone we grew over 50% with nearly £3bn worth of cars bought on site, while £1.8bn of cars were listed for sale through our Sell My Car service. Over 10m customers have used Carwow to help them buy and sell cars since its inception.

In 2024 we went big and acquired Autovia, doubling our audience overnight. Together we now have one of the biggest YouTube channels in the world with over 1.1 billion annual views, sell 1.2 million print copies of our magazines and have an annual web content reach over 350million.

WHY JOIN US?

We are winners of the prestigious Culture 100 award that recognises the most loved and happiest tech companies to work for! We have just raised $52m in funding led by global venture capital firm Bessemer Venture Partners (an early backer of LinkedIn and Shopify) to accelerate our growth plans!

As pioneers, we’re always driving for new territory and positive change, so our work as a group is never done. Where others see difficulty, it’s our responsibility to see possibility – building new experiences, launching new titles and listening to drivers.

Being a part of Carwow Group means championing drivers and the automotive industry, acting as a disrupter and never being afraid to fail (but learning fast when we do!).

Our team of 600 employees across the UK, Germany, Spain and Portugal are revolutionising car-changing and we are fast expanding our mission across every single brand and country we operate in, so jump in!


THE ROLE

This is a director role running the operating engine behind our commercial teams. Carwow sells cars in two ways: Sell My Car, where drivers sell their car to dealers, and Get Your Car, where they buy or lease their next one. As Director, GTM & Revenue Operations you own the operating model those commercial teams run on: the go-to-market process, the enablement and quality that get people productive, the systems they work in (Salesforce and the wider commercial tech stack), the analytics that forecast the commercial number, and the programme management that lands cross-functional change. The function covers five areas: GTM Operations, Sales Enablement, Tooling & Platform, Rev-Ops Analytics and Program Management. You report to the VP, Marketplace Operations and sit close to both the numbers and the commercial teams you serve. You make the commercial motion work; the commercial teams own the selling and the relationships.

This is a builder's role as much as a running one. You inherit a team of three (programme management, sales enablement and platform) and a clear mandate to grow the function to what the business needs. Shaping and hiring that team, and making the case for it, is central to the job. The commercial org has recently brought its Sell My Car and Get Your Car teams into a single account-management function serving one dealer network, so you'll run one operating model across both products (a unified Salesforce, aligned targets and comp, consistent enablement and quality) and get the last of that integration to steady state. The function has already moved real numbers here, reworking the sales process, standing up sales-engagement tooling and sharpening enablement, and your job is to take that further.

You own the operating model, process, enablement, the systems requirement and the forecast. The commercial organisation owns the relationships, the selling and delivery against the number. You design the targets, compensation and territory structures with commercial leadership and you shape decisions through the strength of the operating case. In your first year, success looks like a forecast that's trusted and accurate, new hires productive faster, a consistent quality bar across the combined team, and the platform and process the org runs on every day.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

You will own the commercial operating model and the team that runs it, working hand in glove with the commercial organisation, Workforce Management, the trading leads, and the analytics and data teams that support the whole function.

  • Own GTM operations: define the go-to-market playbook, pipeline and commercial process across both marketplaces, and, with commercial leadership, design the targets, compensation and territory / account structures that tie individual attainment to the business outcome. Own capacity and headcount planning with Workforce Management.

  • Own sales enablement and quality: build the onboarding and ramp-to-productivity structures, a standard readiness sign-off, org-wide QA and calibration, and ongoing L&D for both individual contributors and leaders, so new hires get productive faster and quality holds across the organisation.

  • Own the requirements for the commercial systems and tooling: direct Salesforce as the commercial system of record, owning the process and workflow design, prioritisation and the roadmap to bring the whole commercial org onto one platform, plus the sales-engagement and automation tooling (e.g. Groove), AI-assisted workflows and the performance dashboards the teams run on. You own the requirement and how the commercial org runs on the platform; the platform itself, its build and administration, sits with the tech org, who you partner with and direct.

  • Own revenue-operations analytics and forecasting: produce a forward-looking commercial forecast that feeds trading and reconciles to Finance's P&L view, own the operational reporting that diagnoses what the volume and operational teams are driving into the number, and provide the evidence base behind comp and performance decisions. You own the operational read and set the requirement; you partner with Finance and the central analytics and data teams, who own the build.

  • Own program management: run the commercial PMO, from end-to-end discovery and sizing of new initiatives through governance (charters, RACI, risk and impact), so cross-functional commercial programmes land on time with clear ownership.

  • Build the function: shape and hire the team the function needs across the five areas, from a starting base of three, and make the case for the investment. Run the combined Sell My Car and Get Your Car commercial operation as one, a single dealer view, one operating model, and consistent process across both products.

  • Get more out of the team with AI and automation: mature how the commercial org operates with AI-first tooling and automation, so manual workflows disappear and the org gets the answer without a person in the loop.

  • Feed the operating rhythm: own the commercial-motion input into the weekly operating cadence and the read up to Finance, trading and the CEO, with a clean, leadership-ready view of where the pipeline sits and where it is heading.


WHAT YOU’LL NEED

Please note: We know that no candidate will be a perfect match for everything here, so please apply if you're close to the brief. If you meet most of the essentials, we'd like to hear from you.

The essentials:

  • A track record of leading a revenue-operations, commercial-operations or GTM-operations function at scale, in a marketplace, growth or B2B sales context

  • Breadth across the operating model: you've owned, or closely partnered on, most of GTM process, enablement, commercial systems and analytics, and you understand how they fit together

  • Strong CRM fluency with Salesforce as a system of record: you can set the requirements, shape the data model and process, and direct a platform team, not just keep it clean

  • Commercial process and incentive design: targets, compensation, territory and capacity planning tied to business outcomes

  • A people leader and builder: you've grown a multi-disciplinary team from a small base, hired well, and set a clear bar

  • Analytical and data-fluent: comfortable in a forecast and a pipeline model, and drawing honest conclusions from the numbers

How you'll work (we'll explore these in interview):

  • Fluent and curious with AI: you use it to work faster and help a team adopt it

  • Comfortable running a cross-functional PMO, with charters, RACI and clear risk management

  • Credible with senior stakeholders: you make a well-evidenced case and hold it under challenge, and you influence across teams you don't own

  • Self-directed: you turn an ambiguous problem into a plan, with a bias for action

  • Intellectually honest: you surface the hard truth early rather than the comfortable answer late

Nice to have:

  • Hands-on Salesforce administration or architecture (certification a plus), CPQ, and sales-engagement / revenue-intelligence tooling (e.g. Groove, Outreach)

  • SQL / data warehouse fluency

  • Marketplace, two-sided platform or automotive experience

  • Process-improvement or operational-excellence training (e.g. Lean Six Sigma), especially paired with a commercial background

INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Phone screen with a member of the Talent Team

  • First round interview with the hiring manager focussed on prior experience

  • Second round made up of a case study presentation on a revenue-operations problem (we'll send the brief in advance and give you time to prepare)

  • Situational/company values interview with senior members of the leadership team

  • Final round interview with a member of the Exec team

We want everyone to do their best thinking, so if you'd like any adjustments to the process, just let us know.

WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU

  • Hybrid working: 3 days a week in the office, 2 remote

  • Competitive salary

  • Matched pension contributions

  • Matched pension contributions for a peaceful retirement

  • Share options - when we thrive, so do you!

  • Vitality Private Healthcare, for peace of mind, plus eyecare vouchers

  • Life Assurance for (even more) peace of mind

jobs.title: Payroll Implementation Manager
jobs.description:
Frontline work keeps the world running. Restaurants, hospitals, schools, nurseries, airlines, stores, emergency services. Together they employ 80% of the global workforce, over 3 billion people, and they're among the hardest businesses anywhere to run. By-the-minute scheduling, HR and payroll make them far more operationally complex than the average office, yet just 1% of venture funding has ever gone to software built for them.

 

Rising costs, wage increases, labour shortages and tighter regulation have made fixing that urgent. Sona is the AI-native workforce management platform for frontline organisations, with agents that match staffing to real demand and take the admin load off managers. That's a $500bn+ market the software industry has mostly walked past.

 

We've raised over $100M from N47, Felicis, Gradient and Northzone, signed more than 100 enterprise customers across the UK and US, and opened offices in London, New York, Austin and Lisbon. More on working at Sona here.

 

About the Role

 

As a Payroll Implementation Manager at Sona, you'll take end-to-end ownership of onboarding customers onto our payroll platform, from initial discovery and system configuration through to parallel runs, training, and go-live.

You'll work hands-on with the software itself, not just alongside it, partnering closely with the wider implementation team, product engineers, and payroll bureau colleagues to get every customer live cleanly. Attention to detail and end-to-end ownership matter more here than in most roles, and you'll need to be comfortable double-checking your own work and speaking up early when something doesn't look right.

This role sits within a growing customer function that's still finding its shape. You'll have direct influence over how Sona's payroll implementation process and product evolve, with a level of access to the product team that's unusual for an implementer. Nebuly is a fast-growing, VC-backed startup building the platform that proves the ROI of enterprise AI.

jobs.description:
What is Flagstone?

Flagstone is many things. An online savings platform, reinventing how individuals, businesses, and charities manage, protect, and grow their cash. A diverse group of people, bound by a collaborative spirit, and shared purpose. And lastly, a thriving, profitable business – where smart people do their best work.

Each definition shares a common thread: our unique culture. It’s our pride and joy. And our competitive advantage.

A feel for our culture:

To revolutionise the savings market, we need to be at our best. But high performance takes more than talent – it takes a culture of kindness, respect, and growth.

That’s why we’re building a diverse, inclusive community, where your voice is heard and valued. Where, with close support and room to develop, you can surpass even your own expectations. And be rewarded for it.

We may not change the world, but we can change the world of financial technology. And all it takes is a winning mix of drive, talent, and empathy. Our culture celebrates all three.

But enough about us. Let’s talk about you.

Does this sound like you?

You're a senior data leader who has taken a data function through genuine transformation, and who is as comfortable presenting to a CEO as you are defending a methodology to a peer. You understand what a high performing function looks like, you know how to build toward it, and you have the credibility and composure to hold your ground when the data tells a story that senior stakeholders don't want to hear.

What you'll do

You'll play a key role in shifting the function from a service that reports what has happened to one that drives decisions about what should happen next. You'll work closely with the Head of Data to lay the foundations for a more strategic, consultative model, building the team, the tools, and the ways of working that will continue to move Flagstone from reactive reporting to predictive, commercially driven insights.

This will include:

  • Setting the analytics roadmap, prioritising and sequencing delivery so the function is focused on the work that will have the greatest commercial impact

  • Setting a clear direction for establishing and growing data science capability within the function, systematically reducing low value activity to create the capacity to get there

  • Driving measurable adoption of self serve analytics across Growth, Engagement, Partnerships and beyond. This isn't about publishing dashboards, it's about training, supporting, and tracking uptake so ad hoc request volume falls and teams own their own insights.

  • Rebalancing delivery accountability that currently sits too heavily with analytics, working with tribe leads through sustained and active escalation to shift ownership back to them

  • Leading and line managing Data Analysts and Senior Data Analysts, setting clear expectations for quality, delivery, and behaviour, and acting as the escalation point for analytical disputes, ambiguity, or risk

  • Leading from the front on modern tooling and applied data science methods, and building the team's capability through coaching, pairing, and structured development.

  • Helping analysts understand how their role is evolving, encouraging the team to move from responding to requests to proactively identifying opportunities and influencing decisions.

  • Operating as a credible authority with C Suite level stakeholders, with the composure and evidence to challenge assumptions, and clearly articulate what the data does and does not support

  • Defending analytical methodology under scrutiny, clearly articulating why a model or approach was chosen over alternatives and what could undermine it

  • Exercising independent judgement on when an insight is significant enough to escalate and when it can wait, taking accountability for the downstream business impact of analytical outputs, not just their technical correctness

  • Owning the most complex and high impact analytical work, including methodology selection, assumptions, and interpretation.

  • Ensuring all outputs are trusted, contextualised, reproducible, and aligned with governance expectations before informing decisions.

What you'll bring

  • Significant experience in data analytics, including ownership of high stakes analysis and operation as a hybrid IC / manager.

  • Demonstrated ability to manage C Suite level stakeholders, with the gravitas and credibility to influence at the most senior levels and the confidence to challenge when the data demands it

  • Proven track record of landing self serve adoption where you've led a team through this shift before. You can point to measurable outcomes e.g. falling ad hoc volume, teams confidently self-serving, sustained change.

  • Experience rebalancing accountability in matrixed environments. You've worked in cross functional organisations where product/tribe leadership needed to own their data insights. You know how to escalate, how to hold boundaries, and how to make the shift stick.

  • Experience in building partnerships across functions, not just within your team or your immediate leadership chain, but with tribe leads, product managers, and operational teams. You've driven adoption of your team's work.

  • Strong hands on technical capability, including SQL, Power BI, and Python or similar. You build capability by doing, not just directing.

  • Communication and conviction, with the ability to operate credibly with senior stakeholders and hold the line on quality and ways of working when it matters.

How we reward you:

At Flagstone, the benefits extend beyond false gifts like “fruit and snacks”. Instead, we invest in your health, wealth, and professional development. Here’s a selection of our benefits:

  • Hybrid working - Spend at least 1 day a week with your team in our collaborative London office

  • Competitive bonus scheme - designed to reward and recognise high performance

  • Flexible benefits budget - a pot to fund meaningful benefits for you, whether it's hormone or fertility testing, cancer screening, neuro-diversity coaching or something that matters for you.

  • A range of salary sacrifice options to help you make tax efficient savings on electric cars, nursery schemes, home and tech goods.

  • Working Abroad - Flagstone employees can work remotely from an approved list of locations for up to 90 days a year

  • Mental wellbeing support – Access therapy and mental health sessions through Spill

  • Learning and development – £1,000 personal development budget to help you grow in your role.

  • Private health care - Enjoy all the benefits AXA has to offer, including reduced gym memberships and medical history disregarded

  • Medical cash plan - To help you with the costs of dental and optical expenses

  • Life insurance and Income Protection- four times your annual salary for peace of mind

  • Matched pension contributions up to 5%

  • 25 days holiday - plus bank holidays, well-being days and volunteering days

  • Enhanced Parental Leave – enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption pay.

All are welcome.

At Flagstone, we’re assembling a diverse team that defies our industry’s norms. Think this role could suit you? We encourage you to apply, no matter your background.

As a Senior Platform & Reliability Engineer at Contabo, you take architectural ownership of our shared infrastructure services – the foundation that multiple development teams build on: API gateway and ingress (Kong, Nginx Ingress), persistent storage (Ceph, Longhorn), secrets and identity infrastructure (Vault, Keycloak), edge security and WAF (Cloudflare), and our observability stack. You won't be managing a team, but you will be the technical authority multiple teams rely on: you advise across teams on shared infrastructure services, document your knowledge consistently, and actively distribute it – so that critical know-how never again depends on a single person. At GPORTAL, our vision is to build individual and easy-to-use online gaming experiences for the world. For over 20 years, we've been bringing virtual worlds into people's homes with just a few clicks. Our mission: enabling experts and beginners alike to play their favourite games together with their friends. From Palworld and Enshrouded to Minecraft and Battlefield, we offer around 100 multiplayer games across every genre.


GPORTAL is looking for a Director Marketing who is ready to take the wheel of our entire marketing department, performance marketing, social media, partner management, community management, and graphic design. Reporting directly to our CEO, you will be part of the core management team from day one, with the kind of ownership over people and KPIs you will not find in every gaming company.

In your first six months, the priority is simple: keep the team running strong while you get a real feel for GPORTAL's business, our vision, and where we are headed. You will take full budget responsibility, from managing current spend and staying on top of marketing invoices to building the annual forecast. You will also size up the market to derive strategic conclusions on where we push next.

From there, you settle in as a driving force in our management team and sharpen how the marketing department works so it is well set up for the future. That includes working hand in hand with our tech teams on product-related topics such as checkout flows or game updates and launches. You also take full responsibility for onboarding, managing, and offboarding our external agencies and freelancers. On top of that, you build real connections with the marketing team over at Contabo Group to create synergies wherever possible. Just as important: brand visibility and closeness to the community. GPORTAL is a love brand to its players, and that needs to show up in the social channels and communication tools where our community actually lives.

Alongside that, you own our marketing campaigns with partner studios and the big moments like Black Friday. Last but not least, you advise our CEO directly on D2C pricing based on comprehensive market assessments, both the operative calls today and the strategic thinking further out.

Longer term, you push the KPIs that matter and build retention measures that keep players around. You also shape a team structure that can scale with us. That also means preparing and presenting marketing reporting and KPIs at Group and shareholder level. And you run and assess customer surveys, turning what you learn into decisions we actually act on.

Gaming is a volatile business, and the classic playbook does not always deliver a straight line to growth. We are all pulling for the same outcome for the wider group, which sometimes means short-term compromises we make together. In practice, that also means staying flexible and genuinely meeting people face to face rather than just online.


What convinces us

Ideally, you would have:

  • a strong, hands-on track record leading holistic marketing departments, from performance marketing to social, community, and creative, backed by solid marketing controlling, budget management, and core KPI skills
  • real performance marketing experience, paired with the ability to genuinely inspire a team toward a shared goal
  • some background in IT or hosting, plus experience working with external agencies and freelancers
  • gaming industry exposure is a nice-to-have, though a genuine feel for gaming culture matters just as much as the industry on your CV
  • some exposure to influencer management or social media marketing, and enough confidence to step into a thought-leader role in the market when needed
  • strong communication skills and a knack for handling conflict head-on, with a strategic, analytical mindset that connects campaigns to business outcomes
  • a proactive, hands-on, reliable way of working, comfortable holding yourself to a high bar under pressure
  • an open, global, adaptable mindset with genuine passion for the product and enough flexibility to compromise when the business needs it

  • Build the systems powering our entire customer lifecycle – from first lead to closed customer and expansion.

Drive measurable commercial impact

  • You will work closely with GTM leadership to identify the highest-leverage problems and own them from idea to measurable result.

An internship with direct influence on how autarc scales its commercial organization.

The opportunity to build GTM infrastructure and directly collaborate with our founders and GTM leadership.

A strong engineering and product culture combined with an ambitious commercial organization.

A beautiful office in Berlin and a team that values working together in person.

MacBook and everything else you need to do your best work.

Most importantly: a role where your output can directly influence how quickly autarc grows

Why autarc?

autarc is building the AI operating system for energy installers.

Our platform helps installers manage the entire workflow around renewable energy projects – from lead and site assessment to technical planning, offers, documentation, installation, and ongoing operations.

We already serve more than 2,000 businesses and are expanding our platform across Europe.

You will work directly with leadership, have access to the entire GTM organization, and be able to ship solutions that are used by the team immediately.

No endless strategy decks. No six-month implementation projects.

Find the bottleneck. Build the solution. Measure whether it worked. Improve it.

jobs.description:
Hey!

Imagine amateur football finally had the platform it deserves.
Every weekend, millions of people write their own personal football stories – on pitches, in clubs and on the sidelines. We believe this passion deserves a digital home too.
That's exactly what we're building every single day.


tl;dr

We're looking for a Chief of Staff who works closely with Nik to structurally build out our company- & org processes. 


Main information

  • Start: immediately (flexible start)
  • Location: Cologne
  • Workload: Full-time
  • Team: Founder's Office


Is this a match?

The most important basics – so we both know if it could work.

  • Location: You’ll be based at our office in Cologne (Belgisches Viertel) and should be on site at least twice a week.
  • Experience: You have 5–8 years of experience in strategy & operations and feel confident in your role.
  • Languages are no problem: You speak German and English fluently.
  • Your connection to football: You're genuinely interested in amateur football and have a feel for what moves this community.
  • Start-up spirit: You prefer to play an active part in shaping things rather than just going through the motions – even if that sometimes means tackling things without a ready-made roadmap.


What you'll do - your playing field

This is how you move our mission forward every day.

  • End-to-end ownership of selected strategic and operational projects from concept to execution
  • Building and continuously improving central company processes
  • Close collaboration with Nik on cross-functional strategic projects and prioritization
  • Supporting process optimization in other operational areas as needed
  • Preparing decision-making materials and analyses for the founder team


What you bring to the team

We're not looking for a perfect CV. But you should recognise yourself in these points.

  • Strong process- and structure-oriented thinking, even in ambiguity
  • Experience independently executing projects in a fast-growing environment
  • Tools: Notion, project management tool, Google Workspace, Slack
Good to know
We want you to know what this role really looks like from day one.
  • This role is significantly more hands-on than the title might suggest: you don't just plan, you execute, and take ownership across shifting topic areas. The exact focus will be sharpened further together with the team. If you're looking for pure strategy work without hands-on execution, this role isn't for you.


Bonus

Not a must – but this'll definitely earn you extra points.

  • Experience in a high-growth startup
  • Early experience building People/org processes


The Prematch Setup

We want you to love joining us - and still love being part of the team a long time from now.

  • Employee participation (VSOP) - directly benefit from the company’s success.
  • Modern tech setup - We provide the tools and devices you need to be productive.
  • AI-powered work - We use AI tools to work smarter and more efficiently, and provide you with the tools you need to make the most of AI in your day-to-day work.
  • 27 vacation days per year - For your rest and to recharge. Plus special arrangements if you’re a parent, so you can better balance family and relaxation.
  • Remote work - depending on your distance to the office, you work 1–3 days a week onsite and the rest flexibly remote - whatever suits you best. Tech & Product roles sometimes offer 100% remote.
  • Three cool offices in Cologne, Berlin, and London - true startup vibes to work and grow together. Want to visit another office? We support that too!
  • Remote, even from afar - Whether it’s a week of sunshine abroad or a few days with family - we allow flexible work from outside your usual location.
  • Team events at our locations - Whether after work in Cologne, Berlin, or London: we regularly bring teams together to connect and grow stronger.
  • Offsites with the whole team - Four days out of the daily grind with the entire team: trips, brainstorming, onsite collaboration, and real team spirit.


Still here? Sounds like a pretty good match.

If you've made it this far, we hope we've managed to show you one thing: how we work, what we believe in and why this role at PREMATCH is something special.
Maybe this is exactly the moment you've been waiting for: a team that thinks big, a vision that actually moves things and the chance to help reshape amateur football digitally – together with us.

Now it's your turn.

  • Click on ‘Apply now’ – it’ll only take 2 minutes.
  • All we need is your CV. You can tell us the rest in our simple, short application form.
  • Don’t meet all the requirements? If you think you’re still a good fit – just apply

jobs.description:
Build the Market Leader in Satellite Analytics with us at LiveEO

We are looking for a Senior Product Manager (ISR) (f/m/x) to own the product and delivery side of LiveEO's defence and intelligence business. Sektion 4 builds AI-based ISR capabilities for German and allied defence and intelligence customers: object and change detection in very high resolution satellite imagery, 3D terrain products derived from stereo imagery, and the analytics that turn imagery into decisions. You will run our customer-facing defence products end to end from a product management perspective including analytical products as well as end user applications. You will also build the roadmap that connects different customer timelines, our concept of operations and the actual maturity of our technical components into one plan that engineering and sales both work from. This role exists because our LiveEO engineers build world class AI models and your work will help to bring them into operations and roll them out to many more end users. We need someone who can say how an analyst does the job, write requirements a military user would recognise, and hold the line on what we ship.

LiveEO is a dynamic team that thrives on big challenges and fast learning cycles. We move quickly, stay curious, and genuinely enjoy building together. We are on a mission to break the "curse of Earth Observation": turning incredible satellite data into reliable, actionable decisions that people can trust and use in real operations on scale. 

You will be part of Sektion 4, LiveEO's government-solutions product team. Sektion 4 owns its roadmap and delivers funded R&D projects and defence engagements end-to-end, from research through to production, and sets its own technical direction. You will work day to day with the team's ML engineergs, full-stack engineers and geospatial data egineers, and across LiveEO with sales, pre-sales and the teams building the Twinspector satellite programme. Externally you are in front of military and agency users, partners and integrators, in workshops, requirement sessions and user tests.


Tech stack & tools:
  • Linear (backlog, sprints)
  • Confluence
  • Google Workspace 
  • LiveEO's own ISR and analytics applications
  • Figma 
  • QGIS and comparable viewers
  • STAC-based imagery catalogs Data:
  • very high resolution optical imagery
  • synthetic aperture radar
  • 3D surface models 
  • cloud and secure on-premise / air-gapped deployments
  • agentic tools for a variety of work.


Your challenge

As Product Manager (f/m/x), you own what we build for defence and intelligence customers, and you are accountable for it reaching them.

  • Own the ISR product: take our imagery intelligence application from working demonstrator to deployable product. Define the release scope, the deployment and support model for secure on-premise environments, and drive the first installation at a real user.

  • Run the backlog: work with the engineering team in two-week sprints. Translate operational needs into written requirements and user stories, prioritise ruthlessly, cut scope when it is the right call, and keep the team pointed at what matters.

  • Deliver defence projects end to end: own scope, milestones, deliverables and stakeholder communication for our customer-facing defence engagements, and take on new projects as the pipeline converts.

  • Build and maintain the roadmap: reconcile project timelines, our concept of operations and component readiness into one roadmap that is used to set priorities, not to describe them afterwards.

  • Be the ISR authority in the team: bring operational depth on the intelligence cycle, collection and tasking, and imagery exploitation. Be the person engineering asks how an analyst would really use this, and the person sales asks what we can credibly claim.

  • Work with users and customers: run workshops and user sessions, gather and structure feedback, demonstrate the product, and support bids and proposals with operational substance.


Your profile

  • Professional ISR, GEOINT or IMINT background: Bundeswehr, the intelligence community, defence procurement, or an ISR role in industry.

  • Real operational fluency in the intelligence cycle, collection and tasking, and how imagery products are produced and consumed at a staff.

  • Proven ability to translate operational needs into written requirements that engineers can build from. Track record of driving work to a deadline across dependencies you did not control.

  • German at native or fully fluent level, and professional English.

  • German or European citizenship and eligibility to obtain a German security clearance (Sicherheitsüberprüfung). 

  • Willingness to work on-site in Berlin, hybrid with at least two days per week in the office, and to travel within Germany to customers and users.

  • You take ownership and proactively push work forward. 

  • You communicate clearly and collaborate smoothly within and across teams.

“We drive digital transformation end-to-end - from strategy to execution. Creating measurable progress and real impact for our clients.”
 
Stillstand? Nicht mit uns. Wir glauben: Alles ist BETA und genau darin liegt die Chance für Fortschritt. Darum hinterfragen wir Bestehendes, wagen Neues und gestalten die digitale Transformation unserer Kunden aktiv mit.
Was uns auszeichnet? Wir denken ganzheitlich. Von der strategischen Beratung bis zur Implementierung begleiten wir unsere Kunden End-to-End – mit Kreativität, technologischer Exzellenz und einem tiefen Verständnis für ihre Geschäftsmodelle. So entstehen messbarer Fortschritt und nachhaltiger Impact.
 
Und jetzt kommst du: Wir suchen Menschen mit Neugier, Ambition und dem Mut, Verantwortung zu übernehmen. Menschen, die Lust haben, Neues zu lernen, unsere Kunden zu begeistern und gemeinsam mit uns zu wachsen.


Deine Aufgaben:

Deine Mission: Suche hat sich in zwei Jahren mehr verändert als in den zehn davor. Unsere Kunden, B2B Hidden Champions aus Manufacturing, Industrial Goods und Wholesale, 300 Mio. bis 5 Mrd. EUR Umsatz, merken das gerade: organischer Traffic bricht ein, obwohl die Rankings stabil sind. Recherchen beginnen immer häufiger auch in ChatGPT, Perplexity und Google AI Mode statt ausschließlich auf der Suchergebnisseite. Du machst diese Marken in klassischer Suche und in generativen Systemen sichtbar. Der Hebel dafür ist Content: Sichtbarkeit entsteht heute über Inhalte, die Suchintention treffen und zitierfähig sind, nicht über Keyword-Dichte. Du gibst die inhaltliche Richtung vor und sorgst dafür, dass die Sichtbarkeit belegbar ist, nicht behauptet.

  • Strategie über die gesamte Suchlandschaft: Du entwickelst Search- und Content-Strategien, die klassisches SEO und GEO/AI Search zusammenführen, statt sie als zwei Projekte zu behandeln. Du priorisierst nach Impact, nicht nach Vollständigkeit.
  • Technisches SEO in der Tiefe: Crawling, Indexierung, Core Web Vitals, JS-Rendering, Logfile-Analyse, internes Verlinkungs- und Informationsdesign. Du begleitest Relaunches und Migrationen so, dass danach nicht die Sichtbarkeit fehlt.
  • Content-Strategie und Entitätsarchitektur: Du entwickelst Themen-, Content- und Entitätsarchitekturen entlang der B2B Buying Journey von Awareness-Content für die frühe Recherche bis zu Deep-Content, aus dem LLMs zitieren. Consent-Raten, ITP-Restriktionen und Adblocker haben die klassische Messung ausgehöhlt, und was übrig bleibt, wird dennoch als Entscheidungsgrundlage herangezogen. Bei unseren Kunden, B2B Hidden Champions aus Manufacturing, Industrial Goods und Wholesale, kommt dazu: Eine Buying Journey über neun Monate mit sechs Beteiligten lässt sich nicht mit Formular-Submits abbilden. Du baust die Messung, auf die man eine Investitionsentscheidung treffen kann, und du sagst offen, wo sie an ihre Grenzen kommt.

  • Messkonzepte verantworten: Von der KPI-Definition bis zur technischen Spezifikation. Was wird gemessen, warum, mit welcher Definition – und welche Entscheidung soll damit getroffen werden. Ohne diese Frage kein Tag.
  • Tracking bauen: Du setzt Tracking-Setups in GTM auf, inklusive server-side Container, sauber aufgesetzt auf Consent Mode v2 und die Realität aus ITP-Caps, Consent-Verlusten und Adblockern. Cloud-Infrastruktur, DNS und Pipelines kommen von MarTech und Data & BI – die Messlogik ist deine.
  • Datenqualität durchsetzen: Du validierst, debuggst und dokumentierst. Du erkennst ein Setup, das plausible, aber falsche Zahlen liefert – und du sagst es, auch wenn das Dashboard seit zwei Jahren im Management-Meeting hängt.
  • Von Rohdaten zur Aussage: GA4, BigQuery, SQL, Matomo.Otterly.AI. Du arbeitest jenseits der GA4-Oberfläche und lieferst drei belastbare Aussagen statt dreißig Charts – inklusive der Unsicherheit, die du benennst.
  • Reportinglogik definieren: Du legst Metriken, Granularität und Reportingrhythmus fest und spezifizierst die Dashboards. Den Build machst du gemeinsam mit Data & BI (Power BI, Looker Studio).
  • Lead-Qualität statt Lead-Menge: Rückkopplung ins CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot), Offline-Conversion-Import, Verknüpfung von Marketing-Daten mit dem, was im Vertrieb tatsächlich passiert. Das ist der Punkt, an dem B2B-Analytics anfängt, relevant zu werden.
  • Datenschutzkonform messen: Du verantwortest die technische Umsetzung – CMP-Setups (Usercentrics, Cookiebot, OneTrust), Consent-Signale, Datenminimierung – in Abstimmung mit Rechtsabteilung bzw. Datenschutzbeauftragten des Kunden, nicht als Rechtsberatung.
  • Verantwortung im Retainer: Du betreust mehrere Kundenaccounts parallel, arbeitest in vereinbarten Stundenbudgets und flaggst Scope-Themen früh statt spät.
  • Beratung, die verständlich bleibt: Du erklärst server-side Tagging einer Geschäftsführung so, dass sie die Investition versteht – und einem Vertriebsleiter deine Analyse so, dass er danach anders handelt.
  • AI-native im eigenen Handwerk: Du nutzt LLMs für Analyse, Abfragen und Dokumentation – und weißt, wo AI-Output eine fachliche Prüfung braucht. Bei Analysearbeit ist das ein echter Hebel, kein Nice-to-have.
  • Wissen weitergeben: Du coachst Kolleg:innen, arbeitest eng mit Search, Performance, MarTech und Data & BI zusammen und dokumentierst so, dass ein Setup eine Übergabe übersteht.



Damit kannst Du punkten:

  • Erfahrung mit Substanz: Mindestens 4 Jahre in Web Analytics und Tracking mit eigener Verantwortung für Setups, die im Betrieb stehen. Du hast schon einmal ein fremdes Setup übernommen und saniert.
  • GTM in der Tiefe: Client- und server-side. Du weißt, warum HTTP-only-Cookies über einen Same-Site-Subdomain-Endpoint der eigentliche Punkt beim Server-Side-Tagging sind – und nicht die Server selbst.
  • Consent-Praxis, nicht Consent-Theorie: Consent Mode v2, CMP-Integration, Modellierung und ihre Grenzen. Du kennst die üblichen Fehlkonfigurationen und findest sie in einem fremden Container.
  • GA4 und darüber hinaus: GA4 sicher, BigQuery-Export und SQL selbstverständlich. Du weißt, wo die GA4-Oberfläche aufhört, verlässlich zu sein.

jobs.description:

“We drive digital transformation end-to-end - from strategy to execution. Creating measurable progress and real impact for our clients.”
 
Stillstand? Nicht mit uns. Wir glauben: Alles ist BETA und genau darin liegt die Chance für Fortschritt. Darum hinterfragen wir Bestehendes, wagen Neues und gestalten die digitale Transformation unserer Kunden aktiv mit.

Deine Aufgaben:

Deine Mission: Suche verändert sich gerade schneller als jedes Lehrbuch mitschreiben kann. Unsere Kunden – B2B-Marktführer aus Maschinenbau, Industrie und Handel – werden nicht mehr nur bei Google gefunden, sondern auch in ChatGPT, Perplexity und Google AI Mode. Wie man das systematisch messbar macht, ist eine offene Frage. Wir bauen dafür gerade eine Methodik auf, und du bist dabei nicht die Person, die Folien formatiert, sondern die, die die Daten liefert, auf denen die Methodik steht.

  • AI-Sichtbarkeit messen: Du führst unsere definierten Prompt-Sets regelmäßig über ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot und Google AI Mode aus, dokumentierst, welche Marken und Quellen zitiert werden, und erkennst Veränderungen über die Zeit. Das ist die Datengrundlage, aus der unsere GEO-Methodik entsteht.
  • SEO-Daten aufbereiten: Crawls mit Screaming Frog, Exporte aus der Search Console, Ranking- und Wettbewerbsvergleiche. Du bringst Rohdaten in eine Form, mit der man arbeiten kann – und fällst auf, wenn dir dabei etwas Merkwürdiges auffällt.
  • Logfiles auswerten: Du prüfst, ob und wie AI-Crawler wie GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot oder PerplexityBot auf Kundenseiten zugreifen – und ob sie vielleicht geblockt werden, ohne dass es jemand gemerkt hat.
  • Tracking testen: Du prüfst nach, ob Tracking-Setups wirklich das tun, was sie sollen: Events feuern, Consent-Zustände greifen, Zahlen plausibel. Du lernst dabei GA4 und Google Tag Manager von der Seite kennen, die man in keinem Kurs sieht.
  • Reportings vorbereiten: Du baust die Datenbasis für monatliche Kunden-Reportings auf und lernst, welche Zahl eine Entscheidung stützt und welche nur den Report füllt.
  • Methodik dokumentieren: Du hältst fest, wie wir vorgehen – Prompt-Sets, Definitionen, Grenzen der Messung. Am Ende deines Praktikums existiert etwas, das ohne dich weiterläuft. Das ist der Teil, auf den du später im Bewerbungsgespräch zeigen kannst.
  • Mitdenken erlaubt, ausdrücklich: Du sitzt in Team-Terminen dabei, hörst mit, wenn Ergebnisse diskutiert werden, und darfst fragen, warum wir etwas so machen. Manchmal ist die ehrliche Antwort „weil wir es immer so gemacht haben“ – und dann ist deine Frage die beste des Tages.


Damit kannst Du punkten:

  • Studium oder Quereinstieg: Du studierst etwas mit Daten, Marketing, Wirtschaft, Medien oder Informatik im Master oder du kommst über einen anderen Weg und kannst erklären, warum dich das Thema packt. Wir sind an Köpfen interessiert, nicht an Studienordnungen.
  • Erste Praxiserfahrung: Mindestens eine relevante Station, in der du schon in einem Team mit echten Deadlines mitgearbeitet hast. Ein vorheriges Praktikum oder eine Werkstudentenstelle in einer Agentur, einer Beratung, einem B2B-Unternehmen oder einem internationalen Konzern, gerne auch Freelance-Arbeit oder ein eigenes Projekt mit Kunden. Das ist für uns keine Formalie: Wer den Projektalltag schon einmal von innen gesehen hat, steigt hier deutlich schneller ein.
  • Sorgfalt: Ein Großteil dieser Arbeit ist wiederholbare Messung. Wer dabei ungenau wird, produziert Daten, auf die man nichts stellen kann. Wenn du weißt, dass Genauigkeit deine Stärke ist, ist das hier mehr wert als jede Tool-Zertifizierung.
  • Neugier auf AI, nicht nur Nutzung: Du hast ChatGPT und Perplexity nicht nur benutzt, sondern dich schon gefragt, woher die Antworten eigentlich kommen. Eine eigene Beobachtung dazu ist uns lieber als eine Aufzählung von Tools.
  • Excel oder Sheets solide, und keine Angst vor größeren Datenmengen. Erste Berührung mit SQL, GA4 oder Search Console ist ein Plus.
  • Selbstständigkeit im Rahmen: Du fragst nach, wenn etwas unklar ist, statt zu raten und arbeitest dann eigenständig weiter, hands-on, ohne dass jemand nachschauen muss.
  • Sprachen: Sehr gutes Deutsch, sicheres Englisch.
  • Verfügbarkeit: Mindestens 6 Monate. Kürzer lohnt sich für dich nicht – die ersten Wochen gehen fürs Reinkommen drauf.


Was wir von Dir benötigen:

Mission started?! Dann brauchen wir von Dir:   

  • Deinen CV
  • Welche Vergütung Du Dir für Deine Performance vorstellst
  • Deine Kündigungsfrist bzw. möglicher Starttermin


Warum wir?

Ein Praktikum ist bei uns kein Parkplatz. Du arbeitest an einem Thema, das noch niemand fertig gelöst hat – mit echten Kundendaten, in einem Team, das dich fragt, was du gesehen hast.

  • Ein Thema mit Zukunft: AI Search ist keine Nische, die wieder verschwindet. Was du hier lernst, ist in zwei Jahren ein gesuchtes Profil und du kannst dann belegen, dass du von Anfang an dabei warst.
  • Echte Betreuung: Feste Ansprechperson, wöchentlicher Jour fixe, Zwischen- und Abschlussfeedback. Kein „Melde dich, wenn du was brauchst“.
  • Übernahmeperspektive, ehrlich benannt: Wir bauen dieses Feld auf und suchen parallel auf Senior-Level. Wenn es passt, ist der Weg über Junior in eine der beiden Rollen realistisch – wir versprechen es nicht, aber wir meinen es.
  • Teamspirit pur: Kollegiale Teams mit echtem Zusammenhalt, Hilfsbereitschaft und einer guten Portion Humor.

  • Mobility & Events: Öffi-Ticket-Zuschuss, Teamevents und die Chance, auf Fachkonferenzen mitzufahren.
  • Loft-Offices: Zentral gelegen, modern ausgestattet – mit Raum für Austausch, Ideen und natürlich Snacks & Drinks.

jobs.title: Special Assistant to the CEO (gn)
jobs.description:
IDEEMATEC is one of the world's leading manufacturers of utility-scale solar trackers and the global technology leader in Agri-PV. Our trackers offer unique advantages such as high reliability across the entire lifecycle, resulting in low levelized cost of electricity (LCOE).

As a pioneer of commercial solar trackers in agriculture, our Agri-PV solutions open up a new market segment to combine cost-efficient power generation with agricultural use.

With more than 10 GW of installed projects worldwide, we are entering our next phase of growth. Alongside our international markets, Germany holds high strategic priority as our home market.

Our customers include independent power producers (IPPs), major project developers, EPC companies, utilities, and strategic investors. Together with them, we develop solutions that not only optimize individual projects but make entire project portfolios more efficient, resilient, and economical.

We are growing internationally and are looking for people who think entrepreneurially, take ownership, and want to help shape the next generation of global solar infrastructure with us.

Preparing strategic decisions, bringing the Supervisory Board and Management Board together, actively shaping the company's next stage of growth: a lot comes together in the Office of the CEO that is critical to IDEEMATEC.

You prepare the Management Board's substantive decisions, support the collaboration with the Supervisory Board, and steer cross-functional projects and special topics directly on behalf of the CEO. You translate strategic priorities effectively into the organization and help shape key strategic decisions.

Your workplace is one of our three Bavarian locations: Ismaning, Neusling, or Plattling.

Aufgaben

Strategy & Decision Preparation

  • Independently preparing strategic decisions for the Management Board in the form of decision papers, business cases, and market, competitor, and industry analyses, deriving actionable recommendations
  • Independently condensing complex issues into decision-ready documents for the Management Board, Supervisory Board, and shareholders
  • Independently managing and further developing KPI dashboards and management reporting, including commentary and interpretation of results

Supervisory Board & Governance

  • Central point of contact for the Supervisory Board, and organizational and substantive management of the collaboration between the Management Board and the Supervisory Board
  • Responsible for preparing strategy meetings, leadership circle, Supervisory Board, and other governance meetings, as well as following up on resolutions and actions through to binding completion

Project & Results Responsibility

  • Independently steering cross-functional projects and special topics directly on behalf of the Management Board, including scheduling, resource coordination, and results responsibility
  • Taking on special projects of high strategic relevance, for example in the development of new locations, business areas, or further growth initiatives, as well as supporting international topics and projects at our locations in Spain and North America
  • Leading project teams

Organization, Processes & Digitalization

  • Contributing to the further development of corporate strategy, processes, and organizational structures
  • Steering digitalization initiatives together with Digitalization and IT

Moderation & Interfaces

  • Independently moderating strategy workshops and project steering committees, as well as coordinating professionally with executives and project stakeholders
  • Acting as the link between the Management Board and business functions by translating strategic guidance into the organization and feeding back relevant developments, risks, and decisions needed

Qualifikation

Education & Experience

  • Completed degree in business administration, industrial engineering, engineering, or a comparable field – at least a Bachelor's degree, Master's preferred, ideally with a quantitative focus
  • Several years of professional experience in strategic positions, e.g. in an executive-support or chief-of-staff-type role and/or in management consulting
  • At least one year of experience abroad (professional and/or academic)
  • Proven experience managing complex, cross-functional projects

Professional Skills

  • Solid knowledge of data analysis, reporting, and process optimization, as well as basic knowledge of budgeting

Aktuell schreibt eine Creative Strategist unsere Ads. Du kommst als zweite Handschrift dazu: mit eigener Pipeline, eigenen Ideen und eigenen Ergebnissen. Vollzeit (40 Stunden pro Woche), 100 % remote, direkter Draht zur Geschäftsführung.

Aufgaben

  • Du organisierst den Content, den dein Skript braucht: UGC-Creator, Founder-Aufnahmen, B-Roll, Voiceover, Shotlisten fürs Shooting.
  • Du briefst den Cutter, gibst Feedback und nimmst ab. Fertig ist ein Creative erst, wenn es gut ist.
  • Du iterierst systematisch auf dem, was läuft: neue Hooks, neue Längen, neue Angles.
  • Du führst deine eigene Pipeline vom Test bis zur Skalierung und siehst im Ads Manager, was deine Arbeit bringt.

Zielgröße, damit du weißt, worauf du dich einlässt: rund 50 neue Creative Batches pro Monat aus deiner Pipeline. Ab Monat vier soll ein spürbarer Teil unseres Meta-Spends auf deinen Creatives laufen.

Qualifikation

Wir suchen keinen Brand-Texter. Wir suchen jemanden, der Copy schreibt, die verkauft, und das belegen kann:

Benefits

jobs.title: Creative Strategist (m/w/d)
jobs.description:
Du entwickelst Hooks, Angles und Advertorials, die bei Cold Traffic verkaufen - und misst deine Ideen daran, was konvertiert, nicht daran, wie schön sie aussehen? Du testest strukturiert, iterierst Gewinner und tötest Verlierer ohne Wehmut? Dann lies weiter.

Wir bei BodyFokus sind der Longevity-Lebensbegleiter für Mensch und Hund. Über unsere Marken BodyFokus, BeautyFokus und PetFokus helfen wir mehr als 250.000 Menschen und ihren Hunden im DACH-Raum, ihre Gesundheit aktiv in die Hand zu nehmen. Wir sind schnell, ergebnisorientiert und haben wenig übrig für Bürokratie - am Ende zählt das Ergebnis, nicht der vorgeschriebene Weg dorthin.

Als Creative Strategist bist du der Kreativ-Motor unserer Neukundengewinnung. Bei uns entscheiden Hook und Angle über den Großteil der Performance - der Rest ist Ausführung. Über alle drei Marken hinweg entwickelst du die Advertorials und UGC-Konzepte, die kalten Traffic in Kunden verwandeln - Hand in Hand mit dem Team.

Bei uns läuft alles AI- und Agent-gestützt: Du nutzt KI und eigene Agenten-Workflows als Hebel für Tempo und Menge - Varianten und Copy im Akkord - und filterst die besten Ideen mit klarem Urteil heraus. Die KI ist dein Hebel, nicht deine Ausrede.

Aufgaben

  • Creative Strategy & Angles: Hooks, Angles und Advertorial-Konzepte über BodyFokus, BeautyFokus und PetFokus entwickeln, die bei Cold Traffic auf Meta und Co. stoppen und verkaufen.
  • Ad-Konzepte: Konzepte für Bild- und Video-Ads entwickeln, Creator, Designer und Cutter briefen und steuern.
  • Angles aus echten Daten: Reviews, Support-Anfragen und CRM-Gespräche nach echten Pain Points, der Sprache der Kunden und ungenutzten Zielgruppen durchforsten - deine Angles kommen aus Daten, nicht aus dem Bauch.
  • Creative Testing: feste Taktung neuer Angles und Varianten pro Woche. Gewinner iterieren, müde Creatives abschalten - gemessen an Hook-Rate, CTR, CVR und dem Effekt auf den CAC.
  • Creative Review: Du wertest vergangene Creatives systematisch aus, statt nur den nächsten Test zu starten. Aus Gewinnern und Verlierern liest du Muster heraus — welcher Pain Point trägt, welche Formulierung stoppt, welche Audience auf welches Versprechen reagiert — und schärfst damit laufend den Fit zwischen Audience und Produkt. Jede Testrunde startet klüger als die letzte.
  • Schulter an Schulter mit Paid: eng mit dem Team arbeiten, damit Anzeige, Advertorial und Produktseite als Einheit funktionieren.
  • KI & Agenten-Workflows: eigene AI- und Agenten-Prozesse aufsetzen, die Recherche, Varianten und Auswertung beschleunigen.

Qualifikation

  • Direct-Response-Creative aus eigener Praxis: Du hast Hooks, Angles und Advertorials konzipiert, die bei Cold Traffic verkauft haben - und kannst deine Zahlen benennen (Winning-Rate, CTR, CVR, Effekt auf den CAC).
  • Advertorial- und Copy-Handwerk: Du kennst die Klaviatur - problembewusste Hooks, Open Loops, hohe Neugier - und weißt, wie ein Advertorial bei Cold Traffic verkauft und woran ein Hook scheitert. Aus eigener Erfahrung, nicht aus Plattform-Guidelines.
  • Creative plus Zahlen: Du beurteilst Creatives danach, was konvertiert, nicht danach, was gefällt.
  • Tempo vor Perfektion: Du produzierst lieber viele Angles und lässt den Markt entscheiden, statt ewig am "perfekten" Creative zu feilen. Du weißt: Man muss auch mal schlecht sein, um richtig gut zu werden.
  • Consumer-Gespür und AI-first: Du triffst, was Gesundheits-, Beauty- und Hunde-KundInnen zum Klicken und Kaufen bringt, und nutzt KI als Hebel dafür.
  • Verhandlungssicheres Deutsch, fließendes Englisch.

Wichtig: Bei uns steht Performance an erster Stelle, und unsere Funnel sind Verkaufsgespräche, kein Markenschaufenster. Handwerk und Ästhetik gehören dazu - aber auf dem Fundament der Zahl. Wenn dein Zuhause klassisches Marken-, Design- oder Award-Creative ohne Verantwortung dafür ist, was am Ende verkauft, ist das nicht die richtige Rolle für dich.

Du deckst nicht jeden Punkt ab, bringst aber nachweisbar Creatives mit, die verkauft haben? Bewirb dich trotzdem - überzeug uns mit Beispielen und Zahlen.

Benefits

  • Echter kreativer Gestaltungsraum ab Tag eins: Du besitzt die Creative-Seite unserer Akquise - kurze Wege, direkter Draht zur Marketingleitung, deine Ideen gehen live statt in Gremien.
  • Ein Geschäft, das funktioniert: profitabel skalierend, drei Marken, hunderttausende KundInnen - dein Creative wirkt sofort und messbar.
  • Attraktive Vergütung.
  • Homeoffice & Bürotage im Mix - deshalb bevorzugen wir Bewerber:innen aus dem Kölner Raum.

Unser Prozess enthält ein paar durchdachte Fragen und eine kleine Kreativ-Probe - wir wollen sehen, wie du denkst und Angles findest, nicht nur, was in deinem Lebenslauf steht. Wir freuen uns auf dich!
